skills.author: michaelweissdev

Use when turning a confirmed vulnerability or review finding into a reusable detector, hunting variants across a codebase, or fixing a noisy or silent rule. Not for running stock rulesets (use security-code-review) or for deciding whether a finding is real (use vulnerability-validation).
skills.compatibility: Agent Skills-compatible coding agents with shell access. Examples verified against Semgrep CLI 1.174.0 (Community Edition); re-check the rule syntax docs for newer versions.

skills.author: michaelweissdev
skills.name: skill-security-audit
skills.description: Audit third-party Agent Skills, plugins, and MCP tool definitions for security risk before installation: prompt injection, hidden or invisible instructions, credential access, exfiltration, dangerous shell, over-broad triggers, and supply-chain drift. Use when reviewing an external skill repository or package, deciding whether to install or update a skill, or writing an audit report with evidence and severity. Do not use to review your own application's source code (use security-code-review), to harden CI workflows (use github-actions-security), or to build an MCP server (use mcp-server-development). A clean scan is never proof of safety.
skills.compatibility: Agent Skills-compatible coding agents performing static, read-only review of untrusted skill packages. The bundled scanner needs Python 3.9+ and only reads files; it never executes package content.

skills.author: michaelweissdev
skills.name: software-supply-chain-audit
skills.description: Audit the trustworthiness of a project's software supply chain: whether each dependency and build input is the intended one, is verifiable (integrity, provenance, signatures), and how the build pipeline could be tampered with. Covers lockfile integrity, install-time code execution, typosquatting and dependency confusion, maintainer and package health, SLSA build levels, SBOM quality (SPDX, CycloneDX), and attestation verification. Use when vetting a new dependency, reviewing a lockfile or registry change, assessing release pipeline integrity, or responding to a compromised-package report. Not for routine updates or SBOM generation (use dependency-management), workflow hardening details (use github-actions-security), or auditing agent skills (use skill-security-audit).
skills.compatibility: Agent Skills-compatible coding agents with read access to a repository and optionally package-manager CLIs. Commands listed are real; flags depend on tool versions, so check each tool's --help.
